_meta.title: Heaviest Object on a Scale
_meta.subject: Physics / Mass
_meta.description: Several objects sit on a virtual scale. The student identifies which is the heaviest, building intuition for mass and gravity before formal equations are introduced.

question.text: Which object is the heaviest? Place it on the scale.
question.hint: Heavier objects have more mass — they push down harder on a scale.

primary.questionOverride: Which one is the heaviest? Tap it to put it on the scale!
primary.hint: Look at the weight labels — which number is biggest?

middle.questionOverride: Which object has the greatest mass? Select it.
middle.hint: Compare the mass values in kilograms.

high_school.questionOverride: Identify the object with the highest mass (kg) from the given set. Explain why mass ≠ weight in a non-standard gravity field.

university.questionOverride: Given the mass values, select the object with maximum m. Compute its weight W = mg on Earth (g = 9.81 m/s²) and on Mars (g = 3.71 m/s²).
